title: Transverse order and longitudinal fluctuations in a near-Ising spin supersolid
authors: Mengze Zhu, V. Romerio, S. Raymond, N. Murai, S. Ohira-Kawamura, K. Yu. Povarov, S. A. Zvyagin, R. Sibille, Arianna Minelli, Z. Yan, S. Gvasaliya, A. Zheludev
abstract: We investigate the polarization of the ordered moments and low-energy spin fluctuations in the spin supersolid state of the S = 1/2 triangular-lattice easy-axis antiferromagnet K2Co(SeO3)2 using neutron scattering. The supersolid order develops through successive BKT transitions: the longitudinal order appears at higher temperature, while the transverse component associated with the Bose-Einstein condensate emerges only below a lower-temperature transition accompanied by a change in the interlayer correlations. At the lowest measured temperature, the transverse ordered moment reaches only 11% of the longitudinal component. Moreover, the low-energy spin fluctuations are found to be predominantly longitudinal in character. These results provide direct evidence that the supersolid ground state survives even in the near-Ising regime and exhibits longitudinal low-energy dynamics, imposing stringent constraints on microscopic theories of triangular-lattice XXZ antiferromagnets.
summary: This work uses polarized neutron scattering to probe the spin supersolid state in a near-Ising antiferromagnet. The research confirms that the supersolid order survives even when strongly anisotropic, revealing that low-energy dynamics are dominated by longitudinal fluctuations rather than transverse ones. This provides crucial experimental data constraining theoretical models of frustrated quantum magnets.
main_problem: The study investigates the nature of transverse order and longitudinal fluctuations within the spin supersolid state of a near-Ising antiferromagnet.
main_result: The system exhibits evidence for a persistent supersolid ground state in the near-Ising regime, characterized by predominantly longitudinal low-energy spin dynamics despite the presence of a small transverse ordered moment.
method: Neutron scattering experiments (both unpolarized and polarized) were used to measure magnetic structure factors and analyze temperature dependence across successive BKT transitions.
model_or_system: The physical system is the S=1/2 triangular-lattice easy-axis antiferromagnet K2Co(SeO3)2, modeled by an XXZ Hamiltonian near the Ising limit.
key_observables: Longitudinal ($S_{zz}$) and transverse ($S_{\perp}$) ordered moments; low-energy spin fluctuation spectra; flipping ratio (FR); interlayer correlation parameters ($A_{01}, A_{02}, A_{03}$).
important_parameters: Near-Ising regime, $T \approx 0.35	ext{ K}$ (for transverse order onset), and the small ratio of transverse to longitudinal moment ($\sim 11\%$ or $\sim 32\%$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on separating spin correlations into longitudinal and transverse components using polarized neutron scattering techniques.
figures_summary: Figures show temperature dependence of magnetic intensity (NSF/SF channels) highlighting transitions, and plots of the flipping ratio (FR) showing changes below $	ext{TBKT},3$. Other figures detail spectral weight suppression in inelastic measurements.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the development of supersolid order through successive BKT transitions using polarized neutron scattering to quantify longitudinal vs. transverse moments, followed by detailed analysis of low-energy spin dynamics.
why_interesting: The finding that low-energy excitations are predominantly longitudinal, contrasting with conventional expectations for such systems, provides stringent constraints on microscopic theoretical models (like XXZ) describing frustrated magnetism and quantum phase transitions.
